title: When Gold's Star rises again, Heliostar will shoot to the moon
snippet: Heliostar Metals is planning on quadrupling production over the next 4 years with zero dilution. The market is still pricing it as a cash-strapped developer. It's a 5x from here.
content_html:
Heliostar Metals Ltd #HSTR $HSTR C$1.85 / 516.9m MCAP #goldminer

A Clear Valuation Disconnect

This is a chart that shows where Heliostar Metals is planning on going:

What this means is that if we take the mid-point of this year’s projected production, revenues should come in at $210m assuming $4000/oz gold, and with All in Sustaining Costs (AISCs) at $2,075/oz of gold produced, we will see $100m of Operating Cashflow and nearly as much in FCFs.

Fast forward to 2027 and assuming production hits 62,500 ounces, at $4.4k gold Revs come in at $288m, generating FCFs of $155m.

How do management’s projections above translate into Revenues (blue), Operating Cashflows (green) and Free Cashflows (orange) in a barchart view? Something close to this:

A meteoric increase in revenues, operating and free cashflows, in other words.

Now, mining is a tough business. There are always glitches, delays and unforeseens.

CEO Charles Funk tries to build these contingencies in to his numbers. So far you can see he has been quite accurate:

Even allowing for a hefty margin of safety, how much do you think it would be fair to pay for a company generating FCFs of $110m in 2027, $298m in 2028 and $591m in 2029?

You can buy this business today for less than the cumulative FCFs it is projected to deliver by 2028.

Heliostar breaks even at $1,850 gold, so at $4,000+ gold it is minting money. These projections are based on Charles Funk’s development plan for Heliostar Metals, and so far his projections have been very reliable.

Mines and Metallurgy

We’ll come back to valuation and the valuation disconnect later. Let’s have a look at what Heliostar Metals has got on its books.

It currently has two producing mines - La Colorada in Sonora and San Agustin in Durango.

To add to the complexities of running a mine, we need to take into account the security situation in Mexico; Let’s be candid, it’s not great.

La Colorada is closer to the US border and relatively safe, but San Agustin is in Durango, an area historically affected by cartel activity and more hazardous. Ana Paula, which will be their main producing mine, is in Guerrero and if we changed the ‘G’ to a ‘T’ we might get a sense of what it’s like operating there.

Mexican miners’ countermeasure to this is to invest heavily in security for their mines and employees; for Heliostar, these arrangements are already in place and in the numbers.

It’s not that I mean to be alarmist. These risks and realities are par for the course for most mining operations in Mexico. You could go to many other jurisdictions in the world and find the situation to be even worse. Mining is a tough business, like I said.

Heliostar’s overall mine portfolio is highly economic. The major ramp comes in 2028, when its underground mine Ana Paula starts contributing. It is projected to produce 80,000 oz of gold in 28 for $352m in additional revenues, and over 100,000 oz of gold in 29 for another $445m at $4.4k gold. The capex for this is $300m - we can see this is easily bridged by the FCFs from La Colorada and San Agustin.

Cerro del Gallo will kick in a year later. Its 2025 Pre-Feasibility Study outlines a 15-year mine life, projected to produce an average of 85,700 gold equivalent ounces per year. At $4.4k this will add another $377m in annual revenues and requires only $195m in capex - again easily met from existing cashflows.

Goldstrike, acquired this year for a total consideration of $72.5m ($12.5m upfront in cash and shares, with the balance in staged, mostly milestone-linked payments over up to five years), adds a clean 975,000-ounce indicated resource at 0.46 g/t in Utah.

It is an open-pit heap-leach project with an estimated eight-year mine life and meaningful critical-minerals optionality at the Antimony Ridge target. Development capital is expected to be modest relative to the cash flows already being generated by the Mexican operations, keeping the entire growth pipeline self-funded and dilution-free. Goldstrike is also useful in that it diversifies Heliostar’s portfolio away from Mexico.

Thus we can see a mine plan that scales seemlessly with Starter, Engine, and Afterburner stages, each stage feeding the next without recourse to shareholders for a raise.

Management and Mavens

Management has real skin in the game. CEO Charles Funk owns 2.1% of the company and has been accumulating. The broader board and management team hold another 5% and are net buyers. Eric Sprott sits at 15% and Franklin Templeton at 9.7%.

So both management and the ‘smart money’ in mining are big holders here. More importantly, this combined 20%+ of insider ownership protects shareholders from an opportunistic takeover for the company. They won’t sell out on the cheap.

Combined operational experience across the team exceeds 100 years, much of it in Mexico. The capital structure is clean: 300.7 million fully diluted shares, zero debt, and a cash runway of roughly 36 months with no equity raise required to reach free-cash-flow positive status at scale.

Share

Let’s return to Mr Funk because he will be pivotal to the execution of the plan.

Funk is the founder of Heliostar and has been accumulating shares rather than selling them. His total compensation is modest by industry standards for a CEO running two producing mines and a multi-asset growth pipeline. Alignment is therefore straightforward: his net worth rises and falls with the share price. We can see Insiders have consistently been buying:

Funk is relatively young as a mining CEO and spent the early part of his career inside major mining houses - OZ Minerals and Newcrest - where he worked on business development and discovery teams. At OZ he was part of the groups that found the Ankata and Khamsin copper deposits in South Australia. At Newcrest he generated gold projects across the Americas.

He then moved into the junior space, first at Evrim Resources (where the team made the Ermitaño and Cuale discoveries) and later as VP Exploration at Vizsla Silver. At Vizsla he played a leading role in the discovery and early delineation of the Panuco district in Sinaloa - the asset that turned Vizsla into one of the more successful silver stories of the last cycle.In other words, Funk has already done the hard part twice: he has found economic metal in the ground and turned that discovery into a company that the market re-rates.

Shareholders here will note he has also raised more than $240m across the last six years without destroying shareholder value in the process. The 2024 acquisition of the Florida Canyon Mexican assets and the 2026 purchase of Goldstrike both sit squarely in that pattern - opportunistic, structured with staged payments, and funded without large equity raises.

Florida Canyon (the Mexican assets) were an absolute steal. Look at the FCF they are generating and will go on to generate. How much do you think he acquired these for?

$5m.

So when he says they will look to embark in further M&A from 2030 on, shareholders can rest assured they have a very impressive operator at the helm for further acquisitions. Little wonder that mining’s smart money is backing him.

Valuation

How does this translate into upside for investors from today’s current Enterprise Value?

The table below shows the Enterprise Value divided by the free cash flow the company is projected to generate each year under the Wizard $4,400 gold case and mid-point projections given above.

At the current Enterprise Value of roughly US$340 million, investors are paying just over 3x 2026 free cash flow. By 2028 - the year Ana Paula is expected to reach commercial production - that multiple collapses below 1x. By 2029-2030 the company is modelled to be generating free cash flow equal to roughly half its present enterprise value every single year.

That is an extreme compression of the multiple in a short period of time, driven almost entirely by the production ramp rather than by any heroic assumption on the gold price.

Wizard Valuation Methodology - How We Reach C$8 (400% Upside)

Let me now explain how we arrive at the upside from Heliostar’s current Enterprise Value.

The Wizard process starts with a full life-of-mine discounted cash-flow model at a flat $4,400 per ounce gold price (the ‘unrisked baseline’). This produces an unrisked NPV10 of approximately US$2.97bn, or roughly C$13.64 per share.

From that ceiling we then apply a series of explicit, conservative haircuts:

  1. Operating friction

    • +15% CapEx inflation on Ana Paula and Cerro del Gallo

    • –3% metallurgical recovery haircut on the refractory portion of Ana Paula

    • 12-month permitting delay friction on the underground CUSTF amendment

  2. Stage / development risk multiplier of 0.75x applied to pre-production assets.

  3. Systemic / jurisdictional risk of 22% (Mexican regulatory, security and FX tail risks).

So we have cut down a lot of the additional upside to allow for a number of ‘unforeseens’ happening across the cumulative cashflows.

After these deductions the risk-adjusted net asset value falls to US$1.74bn, which in turn converts to a base-case target price of C$8.00 per share or a 400% premium / 5x to the current C$1.85 share price.

The same model produces a Bull Case of C$11.80 (once the stage haircut is largely removed after Ana Paula is in production). The Bear Case is C$3.70, where severe permitting stall or regulatory impairment takes place. Even the bear case still offers more than 100% upside from today’s price.

In short, the current market capitalisation is lower than the cumulative free cash flow the company is projected to generate by the end of 2028. The Wizard target of C$8.00 simply prices in a more normal mid-tier multiple once that cash-flow stream is visible and de-risked.

Verdict

Heliostar is already generating meaningful free cash flow from two producing mines, is fully self-funding the high-grade Ana Paula build, and is on a clear path to 300,000 ounces by 2030.

The current enterprise value is lower than the cumulative free cash flow the company is projected to deliver by the end of 2028. Once Ana Paula is online the multiple compresses to well below 1x FCF.

The risk-adjusted base case of C$8.00 already embeds conservative haircuts for CapEx inflation, recovery, permitting delays and jurisdictional risk. Even the bear case still offers more than double the current share price.

This is one of the cleaner asymmetric setups in the junior gold space: cash-flow positive today, zero dilution required, and a production ramp that the market is still pricing as if it were a cash-starved developer.

The Charts

The one year chart shows the ‘handbrake turn’ in price following the commencement of the Iran War typical of many resource companies and their underlying commodities.

The share is still in a downtrend with a ‘widening funnel’ pattern. This bids caution.

However zooming in to the 6 month view we can see a basing pattern possibly forming. Yesterday the shares bounced quite strongly and have climbed above their 50 day moving average. They need to get to above C$2 to break that declining channel and break through the 200 day ma for a high confidence entry point.

Thus, while Heliostar Metals is a screaming buy on fundamentals, on a technical view we want to be sure this is not a ‘fake out’ and are putting HSTR on our portfolio subs bench (full disclosure, I already own).

However on a long view Heliostar offers so much upside, this is not a bad entry point for the brave.
